editorial.headline: Storage Space, With the Bali Address Question
editorial.standfirst: Warehouse and self-storage rental is nationally open to full foreign ownership; in Bali, it is not caught by the moratorium, though every address still needs verification.
editorial.body:
This activity is the business of renting warehouse space and self-storage facilities for keeping goods. It also includes the rental of lockers equipped with security features. Its commercial centre is therefore the provision of space for storage: premises and lockers made available to customers who need somewhere for goods to be kept. The scope is practical and legible, covering both larger storage space and the more contained format of secure lockers.

Registration is open at the Menengah and Besar scales. The record offers no narrower category of applicant or additional description of who may register, so the disciplined reading is to stay with those stated scales. For a founder, that makes the early question one of fit: whether the planned enterprise belongs at the medium or large level identified in the record, and whether the activity being registered is genuinely the rental of storage space and facilities described here.

Nationally, the position is clear. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain English, the national foreign-ownership ceiling permits full foreign ownership. The applicable PMA reference in the record is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. This is the national setting from which an investment case begins: an open status, a stated ceiling of full ownership, and no need to imply restrictions that the record does not contain.

Bali does not turn that national openness into a prohibition in this record. Its status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason places it in the medium-high/high risk range, meaning it is not blocked by the moratorium. The provincial rule permanently blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island; this activity is outside that blocked class. One practical qualification remains explicit: the position must be verified for the specific address. Bali is therefore not a blanket bar here, but address-by-address verification remains part of an honest reading.
